title: The School Field
text:
At half past six, the school field belongs to nobody. The grass is wet, the sky is still grey, and the only sound is a bird calling from the rain tree at the far corner.
By seven, everything has changed. The runners arrive first, their shoes slapping the track in a steady rhythm. Then come the footballers, shouting for passes that never seem to arrive, and the teachers, carrying cones and whistles and cups of coffee.
Mrs Koh says the field teaches lessons that classrooms cannot. Out here, you learn to lose without sulking, to wait for your turn, and to keep running long after your legs have begun to complain.
